candidates.name: Kathy Hochul
candidates.background: Governor since 2021 and New York's first female governor; won a full term in 2022. Previously Lieutenant Governor, a member of Congress, and Erie County Clerk. Seeking a second full term on an affordability platform.
priorities: Affordability: refund checks, tax cuts, child care
Fighting federal cuts to health care

cost.label: Inflation refund checks up to $400 per family, expanded child tax credit up to $1,000 per child under four (NYS affordability program)

health.label: 'Invested billions' to stabilize health systems against 'draconian' federal cuts; strengthen safety-net hospitals, keep drug costs down (2026 State of the State)

housing.label: Mixed: pro-supply 'Let Them Build' agenda cutting regulatory barriers AND expanded rent freezes for seniors/disabled (2026 State of the State)

immigration.label: Proposes a state right to sue federal officers for constitutional violations and 'sensitive location' protections during enforcement (2026 State of the State)

taxes.label: Mixed: delivered a middle-class tax cut while 'opposing an income tax hike on the wealthy' (Spectrum News)

climate.label: Mixed: 'stands by the intent' of the state climate law but delayed cap-and-invest rules and is pushing to slow it, citing 'enormous cost to families' (Gothamist)

education.label: Universal free school meals guaranteeing every student breakfast and lunch, up to $450M in monthly grocery savings for families (official release)

safety.label: Sustain record-low subway crime through platform barriers and expanded police presence (2026 State of the State)

repro.label: $35M abortion-provider fund, misoprostol stockpile, six post-Dobbs shield laws (official release)

democracy.label: Signed the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Act of New York, creating state preclearance and barring vote dilution, intimidation, and obstruction (Wikipedia)

controversies.label: First Lt. Gov. pick resigned after a federal bribery indictment; $850M Buffalo Bills stadium subsidy; paused then revived congestion pricing (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Bruce Blakeman
candidates.background: Nassau County Executive since 2022, re-elected in 2025; previously a Hempstead town councilman, Nassau legislature presiding officer, and Port Authority commissioner. Endorsed by President Trump after Elise Stefanik withdrew from the race.
priorities: Affordability: cut electric bills, block tax hikes
Crime: end cashless bail, expand police

cost.label: Pledges to 'cut electricity bills in half' by reversing energy mandates; blames rate hikes on state policy (campaign site)

health.label: Says 'of course' he'd cut Medicaid spending, calling NY's bill larger than Florida plus Texas combined (LI Life & Politics)

immigration.label: Rejects sanctuary policies; touts Nassau's cooperation agreement with ICE (campaign site)

taxes.label: Eliminated $150M in scheduled Nassau property-tax hikes; 'didn't raise property or sales taxes by a single penny' (campaign site)

climate.label: Calls the state climate agenda a 'green energy scam'; opposes offshore wind and clean-energy mandates, favors natural gas (campaign site)

safety.label: Hired 600+ officers in Nassau; opposes cashless bail and Raise the Age (campaign site)

repro.label: Says New York abortion law is 'well-settled'; state Conservative Party leaders describe him as pro-choice (Washington Examiner)

education.label: Campaign spotlights the attack line 'Hochul Is Blocking Hundreds of Millions in Education Scholarships for New York Kids', backing federal tax-credit scholarships (campaign site)

nullNotes.housing: checked campaign site (only a critique that all-electric mandates stall construction), Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, and City & State coverage; nothing that fits the axis; record search also empty, county record shows only opposition to the state zoning overrides in Hochul's housing compact, which fits neither pole
nullNotes.democracy: checked campaign site, Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, and City & State coverage; nothing documented; record search also empty

controversies.label: 2024 order banning transgender women from girls' teams at county facilities (struck down, then re-passed and in litigation); armed 'special deputies' program critics called a personal militia (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Larry Sharpe
candidates.background: Libertarian nominee who previously ran for New York governor in 2018, drawing about 95,000 votes (1.6%) and winning the party automatic ballot access. Marine Corps veteran (1986-1993) and business trainer and consultant.

cost.label: Says government is 'too big, too expensive, and too out of touch' and blames the nation's highest tax burden for driving New Yorkers away (campaign site)

health.label: Mandatory transparent pricing from all providers so consumers can comparison-shop (policy page)

taxes.label: Calls NY's tax burden 'the highest in the country' with 'the worst business climate'; would shrink 'too big, too expensive' government (campaign site)

climate.label: Mixed: Gen-4 nuclear plus renewables; hold polluters 'fully accountable' for damage (policy page)

safety.label: Bail reform via monitored release; 'Community Reform Units' focused on rehabilitation and recidivism (policy page)

repro.label: Personally opposes abortion but says government should not restrict it; wants over-the-counter birth control (policy page)

democracy.label: Expand ballot access for independents and third parties, open primaries, ranked-choice voting (policy page)

education.label: Would abolish the Board of Regents, reject federal education grants, decentralize schooling, and let anyone opt out of state testing (Wikipedia)
